full_judgment:
8. It its Affidavit-in-Opposition the respondent No.2 Janata Bank, has stated, infer alia, that the petitioner is one of the directors of  Modern Jute Mills Limited and he availed cash credit loan facility of Taka 1,90 crore from the respondent No. 2 vide sanction letter No. Jute (4338)362/85/ KMJ:SH dated 22-4-1985 and as per terms and conditions of the said sanction letter all directors of the company including the petitioner provided their personal guarantee as security for repayment of loan. Thus even though the petitioner transferred his share in the borrower company and resigned from the post of directorship an 7-8-1985 the petitioner has not been able to show any paper that the lending bank absolved the petitioner from his liabilities and that the petitioner without, adjusting the dues of the bank resigned from the borrower: company only to defraud the creditors. It has been further stated that the respondent No. 2 Janata Bank filed Money Suit No.4 of 1990 in the court of the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Chittagong on 30-5-1990 for recovery of Taka 2,05,39,182.78 against the defendants including the petitioner. Subsequently, .the respondent No. 2 Janata Bank filed Money Execution Case No. 30 of 1992 on 23-11-1992 against the petitioner and other defendants for recovery of money and the same is still pending. It has been further stated that the petitioner is now Director of MBM Garments Limited which is a sister concern of Modern Jute Mills Limited and that without repaying its debts Modern Jute Mills Limited is now trying to take further loan in the name of the sister company. It is further stated that in view of the aforesaid unpaid loan by the petitioner and the judgment and decree against him, his name was informed to the Bangladesh Bank for inclusion in the CIB list. 

 11. As against, this Mr Abul Hasnat, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2 Janata Bank, submits that the petitioners have provided their personal guarantees for loan disbursed to Modem Jute Mills Limited and that they were share-holders of the said company. Subsequently, Modem Jute Mills Limited defaulted in repaying its loan and Janata Bank and Bangladesh Shilpa Bank and others were constrained to file a Money Suit against the company and other defendants including the petitioners and judgment and decree has already been passed against them. The learned Advocate further submits that the petitioners are the judgment debtors in money recovery case and that execution proceedings are pending. The learned Advocate therefore, submits that the petitioners are clearly bank loan defaulters as found by the judgment and decree of a Court of Law and therefore their names were rightly communicated to the central bank for being including in the CIB List. In this connection, he has drawn our attention to Article 42 of Bangladesh Bank Order, 1972 wherein it has been stated that every bank will be required to send Credit Information to Bangladesh Bank to inform it of the loan and credit facilities extended to borrowers. He lastly submits that borrowers who have taken bank loans and failed to repay the same should be strictly dealt with and unless this Court discourages such non-repayment of bank loans, then the bank loan defaulter culture will continue causing injury to the country and the society and, as such, he submits that the names of the petitioners were rightly included in the CIB. 

 12. Mr Jamaluddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 4, adopts the arguments of Mr Mohammad Arshadur Rouf the learned Advocate for the petitioner and submits that Bangladesh Shilpa Bank had extended the loan facilities of Taka 1,19,000 to Modem Jute Mills Limited and repayment of the same was guaranteed by the petitioners by executing personal guarantees. Subsequently, since the borrower company failed to repay the loan the bank was constrained to tile Money Suit against them and judgment and decree has already been passed against the defendants which includes the petitioners and, as such, they are bank loan defaulters and their names were rightly sent to the central bank for inclusion in the CIB list. It is further submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 4 that the respondent No. 4 is not aware of the petitioners' share transfers in the borrower company as their particulars were never informed to him. 

 19. In two unreported decisions of this court in Writ Petition No, 1776 of 2004 and 2173 of 2004 it has been held that share holders of a private limited company who personally guarantee loans disbursed to a limited company are not defaulting borrowers খেলাপী ঋণ গ্রহীতা” since the loan was neither obtained for themselves nor for their "স্বার্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠান" A guarantor guarantees repayment of a loan advanced to a borrower. The primary liability for repayment lies upon the borrower and upon his failure to pay the same, the guarantor is liable to pay it. It may well be the case that an influential person of high standing guarantees the repayment of a loan obtained by his employee or some other poor person to whom the bank is reluctant to provide credit. If the borrower in such cases defaults the guarantor is no doubt, liable to repay the loan but it would be unfair to an innocent guarantor if his name is included in the CIB list and all banking transactions suddenly stopped. In our opinion, that could not have been the intention of the legislature. In such case no one will come forward to guarantee a loan taken by a person of lessor means. It should be noted that if a case is filed under the Artha Rin Ain for recovery of loan amount the guarantor, if any, can be joined as a party in the suit for recovery of loan money and decree may be passed against, both the borrower and the guarantor but even according to the Artha Rin Ain, the decree can be executed against the guarantor only if it remains unsatisfied by proceedings against the principal borrower. This is to give protection to the guarantor. Similarly, if a person stands guarantee for a loan disbursed to a borrower and if the borrower fails to repay the loan within the stipulated period or even to keep up with the instalments the borrower's name may be included in the CIB list but not that of the guarantor.
